title: Stock Market Sell-Off: 4 Ridiculously Cheap Semiconductor Stocks You Can Buy Today
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions; auto-captions garble names/numbers in places
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA says the post-election slide in semiconductor stocks - driven by fears that newly elected data-centre opponents will slow buildout approvals - is a buying opportunity, and names four undervalued names for November. He explains his method first: forward multiples plus a discounted cash flow fair value. Qualcomm's fair value is $282 against a $165 market price (about 71% upside); its data-centre entry via Meta and Amazon deals should start generating revenue in 2027 and offset smartphone softness from higher memory and storage prices - he owns it and is adding. Broadcom's fair value is $523 versus $326; it builds custom AI chips for Alphabet and other hyperscalers, and slower buildouts only delay rather than cancel sales - he owns it and is adding. Micron's fair value is $1,556 against $799; it has posted 80%-plus operating margins for two straight quarters, component prices up triple digits, and is sold out until 2028 with longer-term customer agreements reducing overbuild risk. TSMC's fair value is $566 versus $395; he calls it the best manufacturing company in the world, with demand exceeding supply, though US-China/Taiwan geopolitics and margins guided down from 58% to 53% as overseas fabs ramp are risks - it is the only one of the four he does not yet own. Nvidia is deliberately left out because he has recommended it so often; it reports after the close on 17 November and he will cover it live for members only.
